adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — State-changing GET with no CSRF token or signed per-user key lets any cross-site or same-origin in-post image (e.g. ![](/t/x/123/unsubscribe)) silently lower a logged-in viewer's notification level on arbitrary topics.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates state (`TopicUser.notification_level` and `tu.save!`) and wires it up to **GET** routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`). Because it is a GET endpoint and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr` now includes `:unsubscribe`, nothing in the shown diff indicates any CSRF protection, signed token, or per-user secret in the URL. A cross-site request (e.g., ``) could therefore trigger the state change for a logged-in user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — TopicUser.find_by can return nil (e.g. user emailed for a mention in a topic they never visited), so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the unsubscribe link 500s.
matched_golden_ids: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same underlying issue: TopicUser.find_by may return nil, and then calling tu.notification_level (or other methods) on nil will raise a NoMethodError, causing a crash/500. This matches the golden comment’s nil pointer concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Every hit lowers the level again (watching->regular, then regular->muted), so a refresh, back/forward, restored tab, double-click or prefetch silently mutes the topic.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the logic is not idempotent: `if tu.notification_level > ...[:regular]` then set to `:regular`, else set to `:muted`. That means a user starting at `:watching`/`:tracking` will be demoted to `:regular` on the first hit, but any subsequent hit (refresh/back/duplicate request) will take the `else` branch and set the topic to `:muted` (since `:regular` is not `> :regular`). This matches the finding that repeated hits can silently further lower the level beyond the intended demotion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/client.en.yml:985 — The page always says "You will stop receiving notifications" even when the level only dropped from watching/tracking to regular, where the user still gets reply/mention notifications.

adjudication.rationale: In `topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, the page always renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` which is `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications")` (client.en.yml:985) and states the user will stop receiving notifications. But `TopicsController#unsubscribe` does not always stop notifications: if `tu.notification_level > regular` it sets the level to `regular`, which still allows reply/mention notifications. There is no conditional in the template/controller to vary the message based on the resulting notification level, so the text can be incorrect for watching/tracking -> regular transitions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — tu.save! skips TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id stays null and update_last_read's auto-track SQL sets the topic back to tracking (even from muted) on the user's next read.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicsController#unsubscribe` directly toggles `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, but nothing in this diff indicates a `notification_reason_id` field exists, is expected to be set by `TopicUser.change`, or that `update_last_read` would “auto-track” a topic back to tracking due to it being null. The shown `TopicUser.change` method (only formatting changes here) does not handle any `notification_reason_id`, and no `update_last_read` SQL related to tracking/muting behavior is added/changed in this PR diff. Thus the described causal chain is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28 — Logged-out users who click the email link hit ensure_logged_in and are sent away with no destination stored, so after login nothing is unsubscribed and they have to click the link again.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `:unsubscribe` to the controller’s login-required actions (`:bookmark, :unsubscribe`) and introduces the `unsubscribe` action, but it does not show the `ensure_logged_in` implementation nor any logic about storing/clearing a destination for post-login redirects. From the diff alone we cannot verify the claim that logged-out users are redirected “with no destination stored” and must click again after login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — The spec passes unsubscribe_url but never checks that the per-topic link is rendered, and there is no controller spec for unsubscribe (nil TopicUser, level toggling, logged out, slug redirect), so the tests pass without exercising the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new per-topic unsubscribe feature end-to-end (server locale `unsubscribe_link` now includes `%{unsubscribe_url}`, `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` passes `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` renders `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` into `%{unsubscribe_link}`). However, the updated spec only starts passing `unsubscribe_url` into `Email::MessageBuilder.new(...)` and (per the shown context) continues to assert only the `List-Unsubscribe` header, not that the rendered HTML includes the new per-topic link. Separately, the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action contains nontrivial logic (creating `TopicView`, slug redirect, finding `TopicUser`, toggling `notification_level`) with no tests added in the diff to cover edge cases like missing `TopicUser` or unauthenticated access. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — The read-modify-write on TopicUser has no lock, so concurrent hits (a scanner plus a click) give a non-deterministic final level (regular or muted).

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)`, then branches on `tu.notification_level` and finally `tu.save!`. This is a classic read-modify-write sequence without any transaction/row lock or atomic update (e.g., `update_all` with a predicate), so two concurrent requests can both read the same initial `notification_level` and then overwrite each other, yielding a non-deterministic final state (regular vs muted). The diff shows no locking around this update.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Saving directly skips the MessageBus notification_level_change publish, so the user's other open tabs show a stale notification level.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code mutates `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` directly. In this diff, the only shown place that publishes the MessageBus `notification_level_change` event is `TopicUser.change(...)` (it conditionally `MessageBus.publish` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set). Since `unsubscribe` bypasses `TopicUser.change`, it will not publish the notification level change to `/topic/:id`, so any live client behavior relying on that event (e.g., other open tabs) can remain stale until a refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5 — Client-side (in-app) navigation to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe only loads /t/:id.json and never calls the mutating endpoint, but the page still says notifications will stop.

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route `topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` defines `model(params)` that loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and never calls the new server mutating endpoint `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (added in `topics_controller.rb` and routed via `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). Since `app-route-map.js.es6` registers a client-side route at `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, in-app navigation will be handled by Ember and will only fetch the topic JSON, while the template `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` claiming notifications will stop. No diff-shown code triggers the actual unsubscribe toggle on client-side transitions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1852 — unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, so any other or future sender using add_unsubscribe_link without that option will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail the email job.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` (config/locales/server.en.yml) to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `template_args` only includes `site_name`, `base_url`, `user_preferences_url` plus whatever the caller passed. There is no default for `unsubscribe_url`, so any `Email::MessageBuilder` usage with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` that does not also pass `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` and break email sending. The diff updates one caller and one spec, but the underlying contract is now brittle and can fail for other callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:500 — The explicit `render :show` added to perform_show_response makes the show action render before `canonical_url` is set at line 87, so topic HTML pages lose their canonical link.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds `render :show` inside `perform_show_response`’s `format.html` block after `store_preloaded(...)`. Nothing in the shown diff indicates `canonical_url` is set later or that `render :show` would occur before such a setup; Rails renders when this code executes, not “earlier” than other code in the same request flow. Since the referenced `canonical_url` assignment at “line 87” is not present in the diff, the claimed canonical-link regression is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — tu` from `TopicUser.find_by` can be nil when the user has no TopicUser row, so the GET unsubscribe endpoint raises NoMethodError and returns a 500.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is used immediately as `tu.notification_level` without any nil-check or fallback creation. The diff shows no guarantee that a `TopicUser` row exists for every (user, topic) pair, so if `find_by` returns nil this will raise `NoMethodError` and produce a 500 on the GET /unsubscribe endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — The new GET endpoint changes state and is not idempotent: each hit toggles the level (tracking/watching -> regular -> muted), so repeat or prefetched requests keep lowering it, and a GET gets no CSRF protection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `get "t/.../unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` routes, and `TopicsController#unsubscribe` mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and saves it (`tu.save!`). This is a state-changing action exposed via GET, so it is not safe/idempotent and is vulnerable to unintended triggering (e.g., link prefetch/crawlers) and CSRF-style cross-site GETs. The implementation also effectively “ratchets down” notification level on repeated requests (tracking/watching -> regular, then regular -> muted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:102 — The slug-mismatch redirect uses `unsubscribe_url` without appending `.json` (unlike redirect_to_correct_topic), so JSON callers are 301-redirected to the HTML URL.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the slug-mismatch branch unconditionally does `redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`. `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is defined as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` and does not include any format/extension, nor does the controller preserve `request.format`/`params[:format]`. Therefore a request to `/t/.../unsubscribe.json` (or any JSON caller depending on the `.json` URL) that hits `slugs_do_not_match` will be redirected to a non-`.json` URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Saving with `tu.save!` directly skips TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus `notification_level_change` is published and the open clients' notification state goes stale.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the code loads a `TopicUser` record, mutates `notification_level`, and calls `tu.save!` directly. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is the method that publishes `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` when `notification_level` changes. By bypassing `TopicUser.change`, no `notification_level_change` event is emitted, so any already-open clients relying on that bus update can remain stale until a refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:90 — The shared `unsubscribe_link` string now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`, so any MessageBuilder caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url` (plugins, non-topic mails) now raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument in body and html_part.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. If `template_args` lacks `:unsubscribe_url`, Ruby I18n will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`, breaking email rendering. The diff updates one caller (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email`) and the spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but `MessageBuilder` itself provides no default/fallback, so any remaining callers (including external/plugin callers) using `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url` will now error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 — The generic MessageBuilder `unsubscribe_link` footer is now topic-specific ("this particular topic"), which ties a shared email contract to topic emails only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the global `unsubscribe_link` string in `config/locales/server.en.yml` to include topic-specific language (“this particular topic”) and a new interpolation key `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `Email::MessageBuilder#html_part` always uses `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for any email that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` (not just topic notifications). While `send_notification_email` now passes `unsubscribe_url`, the diff does not show that all other potential MessageBuilder callers do, so this creates a shared-contract coupling to topic emails and could force unrelated emails to supply `unsubscribe_url` (and may even risk missing-interpolation failures in those cases).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:107 — The List-Unsubscribe header still points to the user preferences URL while the body offers a per-topic unsubscribe URL, so the header and body contracts are inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the per-topic `unsubscribe_url` being added to the email template args (`UserNotifications#send_notification_email` adds `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, and `server.en.yml` uses `%{unsubscribe_url}` in the body). However, nothing in the shown diff reveals how the `List-Unsubscribe` header is constructed or what URL it contains. The spec change only passes an `unsubscribe_url` and asserts the header is present, not that it matches preferences vs per-topic. Therefore the claim that the header "still points to the user preferences URL" is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — The client route loads the topic through the show endpoint (loadTopicView), not the unsubscribe endpoint, so an in-app transition to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe shows "you will stop receiving notifications" without changing anything on the server.

adjudication.rationale: The Ember route added at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/app-route-map.js.es6` (`/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`) uses `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` which loads the model via `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (the normal topic view/show data load) and does not call the Rails `topics#unsubscribe` endpoint that was added in `TopicsController` and `config/routes.rb`. Therefore, if the app transitions client-side to `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, nothing in this client route triggers the server-side notification_level toggle implemented in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, yet the template `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` displays text implying notifications will stop.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28 — Adding :unsubscribe to ensure_logged_in means the email link fails for logged-out users (it is clicked from a mail client), with no return-to-unsubscribe after login.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `:unsubscribe` to `ensure_logged_in` (TopicsController), so logged-out users will be required to log in before the `unsubscribe` action (which uses `current_user` and `TopicUser`). However, the finding’s specific claim that the link “fails for logged-out users … with no return-to-unsubscribe after login” is not verifiable from this diff: it depends on how `ensure_logged_in` implements redirect/return-to behavior, which is not shown here. From the diff alone we can only conclude it will redirect to login, not that it cannot return to the original URL afterward.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by can return nil (e.g. a logged-in user with no topic_users row, such as someone opening a forwarded email link), so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and returns a 500.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, it does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` without checking for `nil`. From the diff alone, there is no guarantee a `topic_users` row exists for the current user/topic, so `find_by` can return `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` (500) on `tu.notification_level`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — A non-idempotent GET toggles state on every hit, so a reload, back-navigation, or email link prefetch/scanner steps watching down to regular and then muted, and the user ends up muted when they only meant to stop watching.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `get ... => topics#unsubscribe` routes and a `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` on every request (toggling between `:regular` and `:muted` depending on current value). Because this is triggered via GET (e.g., from an email link) it is non-idempotent: reload/back/prefetch/scanners can flip the state multiple times, plausibly leaving the user muted when they intended only to stop higher-level notifications. This behavior is directly shown in `tu.notification_level = ... else ...` followed by `tu.save!` in the GET action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Saving directly via tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at are never set and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published; for auto-tracked topics (reason_id NULL) update_last_read immediately re-promotes the user to tracking on their next read, which undoes the unsubscribe.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code fetches a `TopicUser` row and mutates `tu.notification_level` followed by `tu.save!` directly. The diff also shows `TopicUser.change` is the central helper that publishes `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` events when `attrs[:notification_level]` is updated. Since `unsubscribe` does not call `TopicUser.change`, no such publish will occur for this path, so other clients/tabs won’t be notified of the change. The finding’s additional claims about `notification_reason_id/notifications_changed_at` and auto-repromotion via `update_last_read` aren’t verifiable from this diff, but the “bypasses TopicUser.change so no MessageBus publish” portion is directly supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — The unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, so any MessageBuilder caller that passes add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (in both html_part and body at line 90); only the one existing caller was updated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` (and injects it into the HTML). `MessageBuilder` does not set any default `unsubscribe_url` in `@template_args`, so callers must now supply it. The diff updates one caller (`app/mailers/user_notifications.rb`) and a spec to pass `unsubscribe_url`, but the diff alone doesn’t prove there are no other `add_unsubscribe_link` callers that would now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` if they omit it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — The client-side route only loads the topic JSON via loadTopicView and never calls the server unsubscribe action, so reaching the URL through in-app (non-full-page) navigation shows "You will stop receiving notifications" but changes nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` only does `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` and updates the topic from returned JSON; it never calls the new Rails action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` that toggles `TopicUser.notification_level`. Because the client route is registered in `app-route-map.js.es6` for `/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe`, in-app navigation to that URL would be handled by Ember and would not hit the server endpoint, so the UI can claim notifications will stop (template uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`) while no unsubscribe change is performed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — unsubscribe hand-rolls find_by/notification_level/save! instead of the existing TopicUser.change helper, bypassing its notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at bookkeeping, MessageBus publish, and missing-row creation (nil tu raises).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately reads/writes `tu.notification_level` and calls `tu.save!` with no nil handling. If no `TopicUser` row exists yet for that user/topic, this will raise (`NoMethodError` on nil). The existing `TopicUser.change(...)` helper (shown in the diff) is designed to handle missing rows/creation and also publishes the notification-level change via MessageBus, which this hand-rolled logic bypasses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — Generic MessageBuilder unsubscribe_link string now requires a topic-specific unsubscribe_url, coupling a generic email builder to per-topic context (spec had to be patched to pass it) and breaking any non-topic caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/email/message_builder.rb, when @opts[:add_unsubscribe_link] is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)`. The diff changes `unsubscribe_link` in config/locales/server.en.yml to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` in addition to `%{user_preferences_url}`. There is no default `unsubscribe_url` added to `@template_args` (only `user_preferences_url` is defaulted), so any non-topic caller that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without providing `unsubscribe_url` will hit a missing interpolation error at runtime. The spec change adding `unsubscribe_url` demonstrates this new required argument.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:101 — unsubscribe duplicates topics#show's slug-mismatch/redirect and TopicView/perform_show_response logic with slightly different semantics (blank? vs nil?, absolute url vs relative_url) instead of sharing a helper.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicsController#unsubscribe` which re-creates `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)`, performs a slug/slug-present redirect check (`slugs_do_not_match || (!request.format.json? && params[:slug].blank?)`), and then finishes via `perform_show_response`—i.e., it reuses the same TopicView + show-response machinery rather than factoring shared redirect/setup logic. This is a maintainability/architecture issue grounded in the new method, not a directly verifiable functional defect. The claim about differing semantics (e.g., absolute vs relative) is partly supported by `Topic#unsubscribe_url` using `url` (`"#{url}/unsubscribe"`) despite `relative_url` existing, but the exact divergence vs `show` can’t be fully confirmed from the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:500 — Adding explicit render :show inside the shared perform_show_response couples every caller to the show template just so the unsubscribe action can reuse it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `render :show` inside `perform_show_response`’s `format.html` block (TopicsController). The new `unsubscribe` action calls `perform_show_response`, so this change forces *any* HTML caller of the shared method to render the `show` template. That is a concrete coupling introduced by this diff (shared responder now hardcodes a specific template) and could constrain future reuse, even if it may be intentional to avoid missing-template issues for `unsubscribe`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5 — Typo in property name stopNotificiationsText (also used in templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3); should be stopNotificationsText.
matched_golden_ids: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags the same typo in the property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText', matching the golden comment exactly (including noting its use in the template).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:1 — Template placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs while the route/controller/view for route topicUnsubscribe are named topic-unsubscribe, relying on resolver fallback and breaking the file-naming convention.

adjudication.rationale: The client route is declared as `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)` and the corresponding route/controller/view files are named `topic-unsubscribe` (e.g. `routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`). However the template is added at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which defines a `topic/unsubscribe` template (typically used for a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route). There is no `renderTemplate` override or nested route shown that would cause `topicUnsubscribe` to render `topic/unsubscribe`, so the route will likely not find its intended template at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6:5 — Pure ES6/var-to-const refactor of an unrelated route is mixed into the feature commit, obscuring the actual change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes non-functional refactoring in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6` (e.g., `model: function(p)` -> `model(params)`, multiple `var` -> `const`, reformatting), which appears unrelated to the new topic-unsubscribe feature files/routes. This mixes cleanup changes into the feature change set and can make the PR harder to review and isolate functional changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_user.rb:10 — Unrelated reformatting throughout topic_user.rb (scope indentation now misaligned, create_lookup, MessageBus calls, hash braces) adds churn with no functional change to the feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:24 — Unrelated reformatting of template_args, respond_instructions and whitespace in message_builder.rb mixed into the feature commit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:310 — Unrelated from_alias refactor to modifier-if mixed into the feature commit.

This is a style-only refactor with no behavioral change shown in the diff, so it does not constitute a verifiable bug or substantive review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:439 — Unrelated route reordering and silent removal of the post_number constraint from both summary routes are bundled with the new unsubscribe routes.

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb, the diff does more than add unsubscribe routes: it reorders existing topic routes (e.g., moves `t/:slug/:topic_id/moderator-liked` below `t/:topic_id/wordpress`) and it changes the two summary routes by removing `post_number: /\d+/` from their `constraints` hashes (previously `constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/, post_number: /\d+/}`; now only `topic_id`). This is a real, diff-grounded observation about unrelated changes bundled into the PR; whether the removed constraint mattered functionally isn’t provable from the diff, but the change itself is verifiable and potentially impacts route matching/maintenance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/client.en.yml:1019 — Unrelated blank-line removal in client locale file adds churn.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove a standalone blank line in `config/locales/client.en.yml` (between `new_posts` and `likes`), but this is purely formatting/churn with no functional impact or actionable review issue beyond style.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:14 — afterModel nulls details.notificationReasonText by reaching into topic internals to hide UI text, a hidden coupling that belongs in the template/component instead.

adjudication.rationale: The new route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` adds `afterModel(topic) { topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null); }`, which directly mutates a nested `details.*` property on the topic model purely to influence UI display (“hide the notification reason text”). That is a diff-grounded coupling between route/model internals and presentation concerns; it would be cleaner handled in the template/component layer rather than by reaching into `topic.details` from the route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the user has no topic_users row (e.g. shared/forwarded link or a topic never emailed to them), so tu.notification_level raises NoMethodError and the request 500s.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, it does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` and then immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!` with no nil check or fallback create. From the diff alone, `find_by` can return `nil` when no `topic_users` row exists for that user/topic, which would raise `NoMethodError` and 500 the request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — The unsubscribe GET is not idempotent: every hit steps the level down (watching->regular->muted), so email link scanners/prefetchers, page refreshes, or repeat clicks silently change or over-mute the subscription.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a GET route/action `topics#unsubscribe` that mutates state. In `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb` the action loads `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then conditionally changes `tu.notification_level`: if currently `> :regular` it sets to `:regular`, otherwise it sets to `:muted`, then `tu.save!`. This means repeated GETs are not idempotent (e.g., watching/tracking -> regular on first hit, then regular -> muted on a subsequent hit/refresh), so link prefetchers/scanners or repeat clicks can silently further change the subscription.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — Saving directly with save! skips TopicUser.change, so notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at never get set and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published; update_last_read then auto-tracks rows with a null reason and can undo the mute.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the diff shows `tu.notification_level = ...` followed by `tu.save!`, rather than using `TopicUser.change(...)`. The diff also shows `TopicUser.change` publishes a `MessageBus` `notification_level_change` event when `attrs[:notification_level]` is present, so that side effect will not occur with a direct `save!`. However, the finding’s additional claims about `notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at` and `update_last_read` undoing the mute are not verifiable from the diff (those fields/behaviors aren’t shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 — unsubscribe_link now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, so any MessageBuilder caller (including plugins) that passes add_unsubscribe_link without unsubscribe_url raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument in html_part/body (line 90) and the email job fails; the spec had to be patched to avoid this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb#html_part`, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true it unconditionally does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` where `template_args` is `@template_args` merged from `@opts` and does not provide any default `:unsubscribe_url`. If a caller sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without also passing `unsubscribe_url`, I18n interpolation will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`, breaking email generation. The need to update `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` to pass `unsubscribe_url` demonstrates this regression path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28 — Adding unsubscribe to ensure_logged_in with no token-based auth means a logged-out user clicking the email link gets a NotLoggedIn error or redirect and the unsubscribe never happens and is not retried after login.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `:unsubscribe` to `ensure_logged_in` in `TopicsController` (`ensure_logged_in ... :unsubscribe`) and the email now includes a plain `unsubscribe_url` (`post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, implemented as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`) with no per-user/token parameter. From the diff alone, a logged-out recipient following the emailed `/t/:id/unsubscribe` link will hit the auth gate before `topics#unsubscribe` can change `TopicUser.notification_level`, so the unsubscribe action will not occur until/unless the request is re-issued after login (no token-based fallback is shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:6 — The Ember route loads data through PostStream.loadTopicView (topics#show JSON), so reaching the route by client-side transition never calls the server unsubscribe action, and the model promise has no rejection handling for a 403/404 topic.

adjudication.rationale: In the new Ember route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, the `model(params)` hook calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (i.e., it fetches the normal topic JSON view) and does not make any request to the new Rails `TopicsController#unsubscribe` endpoint added in `config/routes.rb` / `topics_controller.rb`. So if this URL is ever reached via an in-app/client-side transition (no full page load), the server-side unsubscribe toggle would not run. Also, the route’s model promise has no explicit 403/404 handling (it relies on Ember’s default error handling), which is a real edge-case concern grounded in the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — State-changing unsubscribe action is exposed via GET (routes.rb:440-441) with check_xhr skipped, so Rails CSRF protection does not apply and any third-party page (e.g. an img tag) can silently downgrade/mute a logged-in user's notification level for any visible topic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `topics#unsubscribe` action that **changes state** by toggling and saving `TopicUser.notification_level` (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) yet it is wired up via **GET** routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`). Rails’ CSRF protections typically do not apply to GET requests, and the controller explicitly adds `:unsubscribe` to `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`, making it callable as a normal cross-site GET (e.g., via an `` tag) for a logged-in user. This matches the finding’s CSRF concern based on the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 — Triple-stache renders I18n output interpolating model.fancyTitle as raw HTML, relying solely on server-side escaping of fancy_title; any future unescaped title path becomes stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: The new template uses triple-stache `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3). That value is built in the new controller via `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, and the translation string includes HTML (`{{title}}`). Because the content is rendered as raw HTML and the title is interpolated into that HTML without any escaping shown in the diff, a malicious/unescaped `model.fancyTitle` would be injected into the DOM (XSS risk). The diff provides no client-side escaping/sanitization to make this safe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — New unsubscribe action has no controller spec, and the untested nil TopicUser path (user never visited or tracked the topic) would raise NoMethodError on tu.notification_level

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil` (e.g., user has never visited/tracked the topic). The code immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and later `tu.save!` without a nil check, which would raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`. This is a concrete, diff-grounded crash path introduced by the new action. The note about lacking a controller spec is secondary; the nil dereference is the verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Notification-level transitions (watching/tracking->regular, regular->muted, muted->muted) have no tests, and the toggle means a repeated GET (refresh, link prefetch) silently mutes the topic

adjudication.rationale: The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (added in `app/controllers/topics_controller.rb`) is exposed via GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in `config/routes.rb`) and mutates `TopicUser#notification_level`. The logic is not idempotent across repeated GETs: if the user starts at `tracking`/`watching` (`> regular`), the first GET downgrades to `regular`, but a subsequent GET (refresh/link prefetch/crawler) will hit the `else` branch and set it to `muted`. This matches the finding’s concern that repeated GETs can silently mute a topic. The diff also shows no controller/model specs covering these transitions (only an email message builder spec change), so the behavior is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:101 — Nothing tests the slug-mismatch or missing-slug 301 redirect to unsubscribe_url, or that the redirect happens before any notification_level change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new controller logic in `TopicsController#unsubscribe` that performs a 301 redirect on slug mismatch or when HTML requests omit `:slug` (`return redirect_to @topic_view.topic.unsubscribe_url, status: 301`) before it looks up `TopicUser` and changes `notification_level`. The diff does not add any specs covering this new redirect/ordering behavior (the only spec change shown is in `email/message_builder_spec.rb`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:28 — Nothing tests that an anonymous user following the email link is rejected by ensure_logged_in and that no TopicUser is touched

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new authenticated controller action `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (added to `requires_login` and exposed via new `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` routes) which mutates `TopicUser` based on `current_user` (e.g., `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` and `tu.save!`). The only added/updated spec in this diff is for `Email::MessageBuilder` to include `unsubscribe_url`; there is no controller/request spec covering the new unsubscribe endpoint. So it’s a specific, diff-grounded gap: no test asserts an anonymous request is blocked by the login requirement and that no `TopicUser` record is modified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — Spec passes unsubscribe_url only to avoid an interpolation error but never asserts the per-topic link appears in the text or HTML body

adjudication.rationale: The diff updates `unsubscribe_link` (server.en.yml) to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}` and updates the spec to pass `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` alongside `add_unsubscribe_link: true`.
